messages:
liz_engineer: Quick heads-up — ran a continuous-batching sweep against streaming endpoints. dumping a short summary + some traces below, curious if this looks like kernel-selection churn or kv-warmup issues :eyes:
samir_perf: drop the run id + command? will try to reproduce locally.
liz_engineer: run=2026-03-cb1, cmd: ./perf/run_batch_sweep --mode=streaming --token-budgets=32,64,128 --flush=eager,lazy --queue=age,size,hybrid --ramp=0,16,32
hao: nice. baseline numbers?
liz_engineer: baseline (no streaming tweaks, token_budget=128): p50=48ms, p95=230ms, tokens/s=120k, kernel_switches/request~1.6, kv_hit=0.82
liz_engineer: eager flush + token_budget=32: p50=42ms, p95=290ms (regression), tokens/s=132k, kernel_switches/request~2.9, kv_hit=0.60
liz_engineer: lazy flush + token_budget=128: p50=55ms, p95=210ms, tokens/s=115k, kernel_switches/request~1.1, kv_hit=0.85
samir_perf: so eager + small budget kills p95 and kv_hit. kernel_switches doubled — suggests frequent kernel reselect during partial-decode?
hao: could be: streamed partial-decode means we launch small-kernel path, then for longer continuation we switch to large kernel; that causes CUDA context churn + kv invalidation/handoff. also small token budgets increase admission churn, creating more tiny batches.
liz_engineer: attached a small trace excerpt (inline):
```
TRACE run=2026-03-cb1 req=0x7f3a kernel=small start=0.000 cpu=0.004
... partial-decode emitted 8 tokens ...
kernel reselect -> large at t=0.042 (kv cache miss, warmup)
stall waiting for kv-warmup 35ms
```
hao: that matches. kv warmup plus kernel swap -> partial-decode stalls.
samir_perf: interestingly lazy flush keeps batch windows open longer so kernel stickiness improves and kv hit stays high. tradeoff is extra tail latency for first tokens.
liz_engineer: thought: implement a small "ramp" behavior for streaming sessions: for first N tokens (16?) prefer coalesce/eager behavior to ensure full batch formation and warm the kv path, then switch back to lazy to avoid p99 blowups.
hao: +1. another complementary idea: add a kernel-stickiness TTL per connection — if we selected large kernel in last X ms, prefer it for subsequent partial-decodes rather than re-evaluating heuristics for each partial chunk. reduces switch thrash.
samir_perf: we should also change queue policy for streaming to be age-based within a small micro-window: prioritize older streams to complete their ramp so cache warms globally. current size-first causes tiny requests to float forever.
liz_engineer: agreed. proposed experiment: ramp=16, kernel_ttl=80ms, queue=hybrid(age_weight=0.7,size=0.3), token_budget=64. run id 2026-03-cb2.
hao: I'll add telemetry: per-request kernel_history (comma list), kv_hit_after_first_n, time_to_first_large_kernel, partial_decode_stall_ms. need a small schema but should be cheap.
ci-bot: perf-check: created perf job 2026-03-cb2 for queue=hybrid ramp=16 token_budget=64. link: https://ci.internal/runs/2026-03-cb2 :robot_face:
samir_perf: next steps: 1) add kernel_history telemetry (hao) 2) run cb2 and post P50/P95/tokens-s + kernel_switches (liz) 3) try kernel_ttl knob in runtime and measure regressions (samir)
liz_engineer: assigned — I'll run cb2 after telemetry lands. expect initial results in ~2 hours.
hao: quick note: watch for false positives from tiny sessions (1-2 token streams). ramp should be no-op for those. add a guard: if expected_total_tokens<=8, skip ramp.
samir_perf: good call. also try token_budget 48 as intermediate. we saw 64 still slightly conservative.
liz_engineer: will try 48/64/96 sweep in cb2.
hao: if cb2 reduces kernel_switches by >30% and kv_hit improves >8 points, we can promote ramp+ttl to staging.
liz_engineer: cool. filing follow-up ticket: INF-2147 "stream ramp + kernel-ttl experiment" and will paste cb2 artifacts there.
samir_perf: thanks — if anyone sees odd p99 spikes after ramp enable, revert and collect kernel_history trace. :thinking_face:
liz_engineer: thanks team :wave: will post cb2 when complete.
